q: What happens when you type a URL into the browser?
a: URL is parsed; browser/OS caches are checked; DNS resolves the host to an IP; a TCP connection and TLS handshake are made; the browser sends an HTTP GET; the server (often behind a CDN) returns HTML; the browser builds the DOM and CSSOM, fetches subresources, then lays out, paints and composites.

q: Explain the difference between == and === in JavaScript.
a: === compares without type coercion; == coerces types first (0 == '' is true). Use === by default.
One listener on a container handles clicks for all children, including ones added later, saving memory and avoiding re-binding. Use event.target.closest().

q: A click on a button creates two items. How do you find the cause?
a: Suspect the handler is attached twice (e.g. inside a function called on every render, or script included twice). Verify with DevTools Event Listeners panel or a breakpoint/console.log in the handler; fix by attaching once (or delegating), then verify one click = one item.

q: Why must every form input have a label?
a: Labels give inputs an accessible name for screen readers and enlarge the click target; placeholders vanish and are unreliable.
Selectors are ranked by (inline, ids, classes/attributes/pseudo-classes, elements); higher wins, ties go to the later rule. Avoid !important and deep selectors.

q: Why does a page feel fast on a second visit?
a: Browser HTTP cache (Cache-Control, ETag/304), DNS and connection reuse, CDN edge caching, service workers. Hashed filenames allow very long max-age.
